title: Matching categories to goals, and choosing how to invest
objectives: Match a goal's time horizon to starting categories.
Pick between SIP, lump sum, STP and SWP.
Explain that these are starting points, not recommendations.
body_md:
The right category for the goal matters more than the "best" fund, and every recommendation must be explainable in one sentence.

## Matching categories to goals

| Goal horizon | Typical categories to consider | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Under 1 year / emergency | Liquid, overnight, money market | Stability and quick access |
| 1–3 years | Short-duration debt, arbitrage, conservative hybrid | Limited equity swings |
| 3–5 years | Balanced advantage, hybrid, some large-cap | Moderate growth with cushioning |
| 7+ years | Flexi-cap, large & mid-cap, index funds, mid/small-cap within limits | Time to ride out equity cycles |
| Tax saving | ELSS | Lock-in per instalment; suits long-term savers |

These are starting points for discussion, not recommendations. Final selection depends on the client's risk profile and existing holdings.

## Choosing how to invest

- SIP: regular amounts from income; averages purchase cost over time.
- Lump sum: for long horizons when money is available now.
- STP: park a large sum in a debt or liquid fund and transfer into equity over 6–12 months, reducing timing regret.
- SWP: for regular withdrawals later, e.g. in retirement.
example: A client has ₹20 lakh for a 10-year goal but fears investing at the wrong time. Put the money in a liquid or debt fund and transfer it into equity through an STP over 6 to 12 months.
say: The category for your goal comes before the fund. Money you need in a year doesn't belong in equity.
An STP stages a large sum into equity so timing worries matter less.
never: Put everything in a mid-cap fund, it's a long-term goal.
This category is a guaranteed fit for your goal.

check.q: A client needs money in 8 months. Which categories fit?
o: Liquid, overnight or money market funds
check.why: Under 1 year / emergency money needs stability and quick access.

check.q: A client has a 2-year goal. Which categories should be considered?
check.why: 1–3 year goals should have limited exposure to equity swings.

check.q: An SWP is best suited for:
o: Building a corpus from monthly income
Moving money between two equity funds
check.why: SWP provides regular withdrawals; SIP is for accumulation from income.
